headline: Microsoft never reviews your app, but since late 2025 tenants on Microsoft's default consent policy stop users approving mail, calendar, contacts and chat access, so 9 of Composio's 12 default Outlook scopes need each customer's admin to say yes; publisher verification makes that request look trustworthy but does not remove it.

notes: Standard OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow at login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0; {tenant} can be common, organizations, consumers or a tenant ID or domain.
No dynamic client registration: the discovery document we fetched has no registration_endpoint, so you register the app by hand in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
Discovery does not list code_challenge_methods_supported, but Microsoft's auth code flow docs use code_challenge_method=S256 and recommend PKCE for confidential clients too.
Client secrets last at most 24 months (Microsoft recommends under 12). When a secret expires, token refresh fails until you add a new one.
Refresh tokens for server-side apps last 90 days by default and are replaced on every use; Microsoft can revoke them earlier.

paths.label: Your own organisation only (single-tenant app)
paths.summary: Register a single-tenant app in your own Entra tenant. Microsoft does not review it. If your tenant uses Microsoft's default consent policy, an admin clicks 'Grant admin consent' once for the mail, calendar, contacts and chat scopes. Set Composio's issuer to your tenant ID, because single-tenant apps can't use the default /common endpoint.

badges.text: If your tenant uses Microsoft's managed default consent policy, an admin in your own tenant must grant consent once for 9 of the 12 default scopes (mail, calendar, contacts, Teams chat, mailbox settings).
Client secrets expire after at most 24 months. Rotate the secret in Composio before it lapses or every connection stops refreshing.

start_here.action: Register a single-tenant app in Entra ID > App registrations, then add Composio's redirect URI, the Graph permissions and a client secret.
On the app's API permissions page, click 'Grant admin consent for <your tenant>' so colleagues never see 'Need admin approval'.
Set Composio's connection issuer field to your tenant ID or domain. The default 'common' fails for single-tenant apps with AADSTS50194.

paths.label: Other organisations, publisher-verified (recommended)
paths.summary: Register a multitenant app and verify it as publisher through a free Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account. Partner Center checks your business, usually in 3–5 business days; adding the Partner ID to the app then takes minutes. There is no Microsoft app review, but most customer tenants will still need their admin to approve the mail, calendar, contacts and chat scopes.

gates.title: Publisher verification (Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program)
gates.trigger: Users in other organisations will consent to your app. Without verification the consent screen says 'Unverified', risk-based step-up (on by default) turns user consent into an admin request, and tenants that allow user consent only for verified publishers block you.
gates.avoid: You can skip it and rely on each customer's admin granting consent (see the 'unverified' path), at the cost of an 'Unverified' label and more admin requests.

wait.note: Partner Center account verification usually takes 3–5 business days, and some checks take longer. Once that is done, Microsoft says publisher verification itself completes in minutes.

badges.text: Each customer tenant on Microsoft's managed default consent policy needs an admin to approve Mail.Read/ReadWrite, Calendars.*, Contacts.ReadWrite, Chat.ReadWrite and MailboxSettings.*. Verification does not remove this.
Needs a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account (the partner global account for your organisation). Microsoft charges nothing for it.
Partner Center checks that your business is legally registered at the stated address.
The domain of your Partner Center email must match the app's publisher domain or a DNS-verified domain in your tenant. *.onmicrosoft.com does not count.
Client secrets expire after at most 24 months. Rotate the secret in Composio before it lapses or every connection stops refreshing.

start_here.action: Start Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program enrolment in Partner Center with a business email at your own domain. Verification usually takes 3–5 business days.
Register a multitenant app, verify your domain and set it as publisher domain, grant admin consent in your own tenant, and build against your own mailbox.
Add your Partner One ID under Branding & properties > Add Partner ID to verify publisher. It completes in minutes.
Send the customer's IT admin the admin-consent link and request message we drafted.

paths.label: Other organisations, not publisher-verified
paths.summary: Register a multitenant app and skip publisher verification. Nothing stops you technically, but the consent screen says 'Unverified' and, in practice, every customer's admin must grant consent before their users can connect.

badges.text: Expect an admin in almost every customer tenant. Microsoft's default policy blocks user consent for 9 of the 12 default scopes, and risk-based step-up (on by default) turns user consent for unverified multitenant apps into an admin request.
Client secrets expire after at most 24 months. Rotate the secret in Composio before it lapses or every connection stops refreshing.

start_here.action: Register a multitenant app, add Composio's redirect URI, the Graph permissions and a client secret, and grant admin consent in your own tenant.
Send the customer's IT admin the admin-consent link and request message we drafted.

start_here.when: When admin requests start slowing deals
start_here.action: Move to the publisher-verified path; it adds a blue verified badge with no code changes.

paths.label: Enterprise trust: Microsoft 365 Certification (optional)
paths.summary: Optional for enterprise sales. After publisher verification, complete Publisher Attestation, then a paid independent audit (Microsoft 365 Certification) that you repeat every year. Microsoft does not require it for Graph access, but it says some tenants may require it before enabling an app.

gates.title: Publisher verification (Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program)
gates.trigger: Microsoft 365 Certification requires a publisher-verified app.

wait.note: Partner Center account verification usually takes 3–5 business days, and some checks take longer. Publisher verification itself completes in minutes after that.

gates.title: Microsoft 365 Certification audit
gates.trigger: You choose to certify, usually because enterprise customers ask for it.
gates.avoid: It is optional: skip it unless customers require it.

wait.note: Microsoft sets deadlines for you (14 days for the document stage, 60 days for evidence, one extension of up to 60 days) but publishes no review turnaround.

gates.title: Yearly recertification
gates.trigger: Every year after you are certified.

badges.text: You pay the audit firm (Claranet) for the audit, plus a pen test at extra cost if you lack a third-party pen test from the last 12 months.
Needs a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account (the partner global account for your organisation).
Partner Center checks that your business is legally registered at the stated address.
Microsoft's managed consent policy lists no exception for certified apps, so expect customer admins to still approve the mail, calendar, contacts and chat scopes.

start_here.action: Start Partner Center enrolment and publisher verification, exactly as on the publisher-verified path.
Complete Publisher Attestation in Partner Center (Microsoft says most take an hour or less).
Select 'Start Certification' in Partner Center, set up the Claranet account, and plan for a 14-day document stage, a 60-day evidence stage and yearly recertification.

scopes.what: Read the user's calendars. Graph marks it as not needing admin consent, but Microsoft's managed default consent policy excludes it from user consent, so expect an admin to approve.
Create, read, update and delete events in the user's calendars. User-consentable per Graph, but excluded by Microsoft's managed default policy.
Read and write calendars the user can access, including shared and delegate calendars. User-consentable per Graph, but excluded by Microsoft's managed default policy.
Full access to the user's contacts. User-consentable per Graph, but excluded by Microsoft's managed default policy.

Read and write the user's Teams 1:1 and group chats (not mail). User-consentable per Graph, but excluded by Microsoft's managed default policy. Unlike the mail and calendar scopes, Graph's reference does not mark it as available for personal Microsoft accounts. Drop it if your agent doesn't need Teams chats.
Read the user's mailbox. User-consentable per Graph, but excluded by Microsoft's managed default policy.
Create, read, update and delete the user's mail (sending needs Mail.Send). User-consentable per Graph, but excluded by Microsoft's managed default policy.

Send mail as the signed-in user. Not on the managed policy's exclusion list, so users can approve it unless their tenant turns user consent off or the app is an unverified multitenant app caught by risk-based step-up.
Read the user's mailbox settings (time zone, automatic replies and similar). User-consentable per Graph, but excluded by Microsoft's managed default policy.
Read and change the user's mailbox settings. User-consentable per Graph, but excluded by Microsoft's managed default policy.
Lets Composio get refresh tokens so access continues when the user is away. Grants no extra data access; user-consentable.
Sign the user in and read their basic profile. User-consentable.

prerequisites.item: A Microsoft Entra work account with at least the Application Developer role, in your company's own tenant
prerequisites.why: App registrations live in a tenant. Personal Microsoft accounts land in Microsoft's shared tenant, and apps registered with them can't be publisher-verified.

prerequisites.item: Someone in your tenant with Cloud Application Administrator, Application Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator
prerequisites.why: Needed to grant admin consent in your own tenant and, for publisher verification, to add the Partner ID.

prerequisites.item: A company domain you control (DNS access) and a business email address at that domain
prerequisites.why: Publisher verification needs your Partner Center email domain to match a verified domain on the app; free email addresses are not accepted.
Partner Center verification checks your business registration and address before you get a usable Partner One ID.

steps.title: Sign in with a work account in your company's Entra tenant
steps.detail: Use a Microsoft Entra work or school account with at least the Application Developer role. Don't use a personal Outlook.com or Hotmail account: it signs you into Microsoft's shared 'Microsoft Services' tenant, where you can't manage apps, and apps registered with a personal account can't be publisher-verified. No tenant yet? Creating a free Azure account creates one and makes you Global Administrator.

steps.title: Register the app and choose who can sign in
steps.detail: Go to Entra ID > App registrations > New registration. Use your product name (users see it on the consent screen). Under Supported account types pick 'Single tenant only' for your own organisation, 'Multiple Entra ID tenants' for other organisations' work accounts, or 'Any Entra ID Tenant + Personal Microsoft accounts' if Outlook.com users should connect too. Choose carefully: Microsoft's troubleshooting guide says to re-create the registration if the account type is wrong. Copy the Application (client) ID from Overview.

paste.label: Supported account type (other organisations, work accounts)
Supported account type (other organisations + Outlook.com)
paste.value: Any Entra ID Tenant + Personal Microsoft accounts

steps.title: Add Composio's callback as a Web redirect URI
steps.detail: In your app registration go to Manage > Authentication > Add Redirect URI > Web, paste the URI below and save. It must exactly match the redirect URI set in your Composio auth config. If you leave the auth config's redirect field at the toolkit default, register the legacy https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add instead. A mismatch shows up as AADSTS50011.

steps.title: Create a client secret and note its expiry date
steps.detail: Go to Certificates & secrets > Client secrets > New client secret. Pick an expiry: the maximum is 24 months and Microsoft recommends under 12. Copy the secret's Value (not the Secret ID); it is shown only once. Add a calendar reminder before the expiry date, because token refresh fails for every user once the secret lapses.

steps.title: Add the Microsoft Graph delegated permissions
steps.detail: Go to API permissions > Add a permission > Microsoft Graph > Delegated permissions and add the scopes your Composio auth config requests (Composio's 12 defaults are below). An admin approves exactly what is listed here, and Microsoft says every permission must be listed for the admin consent flow to work. Trim what you don't need: of the 12 defaults, only Mail.Send, User.Read and offline_access are outside the exclusion list of Microsoft's managed default consent policy.

paste.label: Composio default scopes
paste.value: Calendars.Read Calendars.ReadWrite Calendars.ReadWrite.Shared Contacts.ReadWrite Chat.ReadWrite Mail.Read Mail.ReadWrite Mail.Send MailboxSettings.Read MailboxSettings.ReadWrite offline_access User.Read

paste.label: Smallest set users can usually approve themselves (send-only agent)

steps.title: Grant admin consent in your own tenant
steps.detail: On API permissions, select 'Grant admin consent for <your tenant>' and confirm. This needs Cloud Application Administrator, Application Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator. You and your colleagues can then connect without the 'Need admin approval' screen, and you can test the whole flow today.

steps.title: Verify your company domain and set it as the publisher domain
steps.detail: In the Entra admin center add your domain under Custom domain names, create the TXT record at your registrar and select Verify (DNS can take from minutes to a few days). Then open App registrations > your app > Branding & properties and set Publisher domain to that verified domain. It must match the domain of the email you use in Partner Center; *.onmicrosoft.com can't be used.

steps.title: Join the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program and pass verification
steps.detail: In Partner Center, enrol with a work account from your primary tenant and a business email at your domain (no free email). Microsoft checks your legal registration, your email and your domain or employment documents, usually in 3–5 business days. Track it under Account settings > Legal info > Verification Summary. Then copy the Partner One ID of type PartnerGlobal (a location ID will not work).

steps.title: Add your Partner One ID to the app
steps.detail: Sign in with multifactor authentication as an Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator who is also a Partner Admin or Account Admin in Partner Center. Open App registrations > your app > Branding & properties > Add Partner ID to verify publisher, enter the Partner One ID and select Verify and save. It takes a few minutes; the blue verified badge then appears on the consent screen.

steps.title: Send each customer's admin a one-click consent link
steps.detail: For each customer organisation, send its IT admin the link below with your client ID filled in. 'organizations' makes the consent land in the admin's own tenant. The admin needs Cloud Application Administrator, Application Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator. After they approve, users connect normally; nothing changes in Composio.

paste.label: Message to the customer's IT admin
paste.value: Hi, <Product> connects to Outlook through Microsoft Graph so it can read, draft and send email and manage calendar events for users who connect their own account. Your tenant requires an admin to approve these delegated permissions (each user only grants access to their own data): Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send, Calendars.Read, Calendars.ReadWrite, Calendars.ReadWrite.Shared, Contacts.ReadWrite, Chat.ReadWrite, MailboxSettings.Read, MailboxSettings.ReadWrite, User.Read, offline_access. You can review and approve in one step here: <admin consent URL>. It needs the Cloud Application Administrator, Application Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator role. Publisher: <Company>.

steps.title: Test the consent screen from another tenant
steps.detail: Connect through Composio with a user from a different tenant, and with an Outlook.com account if you support personal accounts. Check what they see: 'Unverified' or your verified publisher name, and whether 'Need admin approval' appears. Don't use the in-flow 'sign in as an admin' option as your main fix: it may connect the admin's mailbox instead of the user's.

steps.title: Complete Publisher Attestation in Partner Center
steps.detail: Answer Microsoft's self-assessment questions on your security and data handling. Microsoft says most attestations take an hour or less. If your submission is more than three months old when you start certification, you must resubmit it.

steps.title: Start Microsoft 365 Certification and complete the audit
steps.detail: In Partner Center select 'Start Certification' and set up your account with Claranet, the audit firm you pay. Upload architecture, data-flow and inventory documents within 14 days, then provide evidence for every in-scope control within 60 days (one extension of up to 60 days is possible). You need a third-party pen test from the last 12 months, or the auditor runs one at extra cost. Recertify every year.

while_you_wait.text: Build and test against your own tenant while Partner Center verification runs: register the app, grant admin consent there and connect your own mailbox.
There is no test mode or user cap. Pilot customers can connect as soon as their admin approves your app, before you are publisher-verified.
Composio's managed Outlook app works for prototypes now, but you can't send customers an admin-consent link for it because Composio does not publish its client ID.
Put your client secret's expiry date in the calendar now and rotate it before it lapses.

blockers.symptom: Users see 'Need admin approval' or 'Approval required', or the connection fails with AADSTS90094 or AADSTS65001.
blockers.cause: The user's tenant won't let them consent to the scopes you request. Since late 2025, tenants on Microsoft's managed default consent policy block user consent for Mail.Read/ReadWrite, Calendars.*, Contacts.ReadWrite, Chat.ReadWrite and MailboxSettings.*. Some tenants turn user consent off entirely.
blockers.fix_now: Ask that tenant's admin to approve once, using the admin-consent link for your client ID or Enterprise apps > your app > Permissions > Grant admin consent. Then the user starts a fresh connection.
blockers.fix_properly: Request only the scopes you need (Mail.Send, User.Read and offline_access avoid the default policy's block), ask customers to turn on the admin consent workflow so users can send requests, and get publisher-verified so admins trust the request.

escalate.how: This is the customer's decision, not Microsoft's. Contact the customer's Microsoft 365 or Entra admin.
escalate.draft: Hi <admin>, <user> is trying to connect Outlook to <Product> and sees 'Need admin approval'. Your tenant requires an admin to approve these Microsoft Graph delegated permissions: <scopes>. You can review and approve in one step here: https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations/adminconsent?client_id=<client_id> (needs Cloud Application Administrator or Application Administrator). After that, users can connect themselves.

blockers.symptom: The consent screen shows 'Unverified', or users get AADSTS900941: 'Administrator consent is required. App is considered risky.'
blockers.cause: Your multitenant app isn't publisher-verified. Risk-based step-up consent, on by default, treats user consent to newly registered, unverified multitenant apps asking for more than basic sign-in as risky and sends it to an admin.
blockers.fix_now: Have the tenant's admin grant consent with the admin-consent link.

escalate.how: Only the customer's admin can approve. Microsoft support will not override a tenant's consent settings.
escalate.draft: Hi <admin>, <Product> shows as 'Unverified' while our Microsoft publisher verification is in progress, so your tenant asks for admin approval. Please review the requested permissions and approve here if you are comfortable: https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations/adminconsent?client_id=<client_id>

blockers.symptom: 'Verify and save' fails with PublisherDomainMismatch, MPNAccountNotVetted or 'A verified publisher cannot be added to this application'.
blockers.cause: The app's publisher domain doesn't match the domain of your Partner Center primary contact's email, your Partner Center account hasn't finished verification, you used a location Partner ID instead of the partner global one, or Microsoft's risk check flagged the request.
blockers.fix_now: Check that Partner Center > Account settings > Legal info > Verification Summary is complete, use the PartnerGlobal ID, and set the publisher domain to your verified email domain. If the request was flagged as risky, retry the next day.
blockers.fix_properly: Register the app in the tenant linked to your partner global account, using a work account that holds both required roles and signs in with MFA.

escalate.how: In Partner Center, open the AI assistant and select Contact Support.
escalate.draft: Our Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account (Partner One ID <id>, PartnerGlobal) is used for publisher verification of Entra app <app object ID>. 'Verify and save' fails with <error code>. Verification Summary shows <status>. What is still pending on our account?

blockers.symptom: Connecting fails with AADSTS50194 (the app 'isn't configured as a multitenant application. Usage of the /common endpoint isn't supported') or, for someone outside your organisation, AADSTS50020 ('User account ... does not exist in tenant').
blockers.cause: Composio sends users to the /common endpoint by default, which single-tenant apps can't use. Single-tenant apps also accept only accounts from your own tenant.
blockers.fix_now: Set the connection's issuer field to your tenant ID or primary domain. If one of your own users gets AADSTS50020, have them sign in again in a private window with the right account.
blockers.fix_properly: If people outside your organisation must connect, register a multitenant app instead.

escalate.how: Post on Microsoft Q&A with the Microsoft Entra ID tag, including the full AADSTS code and correlation ID.
escalate.draft: Single-tenant Entra app (client ID <id>) used for delegated Microsoft Graph access via a third-party OAuth broker. Sign-in fails with <AADSTS code>. Authority used: <https://login.microsoftonline.com/...>. Correlation ID: <id>. What should the authority be for a single-tenant app?

blockers.symptom: AADSTS50011: 'The redirect URI ... specified in the request does not match the redirect URIs configured for the application'.
blockers.cause: The callback URL Composio sends is not registered, exactly, as a Web redirect URI on your app registration.
blockers.fix_now: Copy the URI from the error into Authentication > Add Redirect URI > Web, save, and wait three to five minutes before retrying.
blockers.fix_properly: Keep the redirect URI in your Composio auth config and in Entra identical, including any trailing slash.

escalate.how: Post on Microsoft Q&A with the Microsoft Entra ID tag if the URI matches and the error persists.
escalate.draft: AADSTS50011 for app <client ID>. The request's redirect_uri is <uri>; the app registration lists <uris> under the Web platform. Waited 5 minutes after saving. What else must match?

checks.detail: Anyone with at least the Application Developer role registers an app in Entra ID > App registrations, with no Microsoft review.

Microsoft never reviews the app, but each customer tenant decides: its default policy blocks user consent for mail, calendar, contacts and chat scopes, and risk-based step-up sends unverified multitenant apps to admin consent.
Graph marks some permissions admin-only. All 12 Composio defaults are marked user-consentable, but Microsoft's managed default policy excludes 9 of them from user consent.
No Microsoft app, scope or marketplace review is needed for Graph OAuth. Publisher verification is an identity check, and Microsoft 365 Certification is optional.
Not required by Microsoft. Microsoft 365 Certification (a yearly independent audit) is optional, though Microsoft says some tenants may require it before enabling an app.
No caps on users, tenants or connections found. Rate limits apply per app per mailbox (10,000 requests per 10 minutes, four concurrent requests).
Not for a basic app. Publisher verification needs a verified Partner Center account for a legally registered business, a work account, and a verified domain matching your Partner Center email.
Publisher verification requires joining the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program, which Microsoft says is free for this. Microsoft 365 Certification is paid to the audit firm.
There is no test mode: the app works for any allowed account once registered. Watch client secret expiry (24 months maximum) and 90-day refresh tokens.
Partner Center verification usually takes 3–5 business days; publisher verification then takes minutes. Customer admin approval has no timeline.
Partner Center support for partner verification, Azure support or Microsoft Q&A for Entra issues, appcert@microsoft.com for certification. Consent is the customer's admin's call.

unknowns.question: Which consent setting each customer's tenant uses (Microsoft-managed default, verified publishers and low-impact only, the legacy 'allow user consent', or user consent off).
unknowns.why: It decides, customer by customer, whether users can approve your app themselves or must wait for their admin.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Ask the customer's admin to check Entra ID > Enterprise apps > Consent and permissions > User consent settings, or test a connection from that tenant.

unknowns.question: Whether requesting Chat.ReadWrite breaks consent for personal Microsoft accounts (Outlook.com).
unknowns.why: Composio's defaults include Chat.ReadWrite, which Graph's reference does not mark as available for personal accounts. If it errors, Outlook.com users can't connect with the default scopes.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Connect a personal Outlook.com account with the default scopes. If it fails, remove Chat.ReadWrite (Teams chats) from the auth config scopes.

unknowns.question: Whether Composio's managed Outlook app is publisher-verified.
unknowns.why: If it isn't, users in other tenants hit risk-based step-up on the managed app as well, which is a reason to bring your own verified app sooner.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Connect with the managed app from another tenant and look for a blue verified badge or 'Unverified' on the consent screen, or ask Composio support.

unknowns.question: Whether Microsoft 365 Certification or Publisher Attestation changes how Microsoft's managed consent policy treats an app.
unknowns.why: If certified apps were exempt, certification would remove the per-customer admin step. We found no source saying so.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Email appcert@microsoft.com, and watch the exclusion list on Microsoft's 'Manage app consent policies' page.

unknowns.question: Whether Microsoft will add more scopes (for example Mail.Send) to the managed policy's exclusion list.
unknowns.why: Mail.Send, User.Read and offline_access are the only Composio defaults users can still approve under the default policy, and Microsoft updates that policy automatically.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Recheck the 'Microsoft recommended current settings' section of Manage app consent policies and Microsoft 365 Message Center posts every quarter.

composio_notes.text: Composio's Outlook auth config takes client_id, client_secret, optional scopes (the 12 Graph defaults), oauth_redirect_uri and microsoft_cloud ('global' for commercial Microsoft 365, 'gcc_high' for US Government GCC High). Each connection takes an optional issuer: a tenant alias, tenant ID or domain, defaulting to 'common'.
For a single-tenant app, set issuer to your tenant ID or domain. The default 'common' fails for single-tenant apps with AADSTS50194.
Composio does not publish the client ID of its managed Outlook app, so you can't send customers a direct admin-consent link for it. With your own app you can.

Adding permissions to the app registration is not admin consent. Once a tenant admin grants consent, each user starts a fresh connection; nothing changes on Composio's side. Auth links expire after about 10 minutes.
If you add scopes later, users must reconnect, and under Microsoft's managed policy new or broader permissions need admin approval again.
Composio says a verified publisher can reduce consent friction but does not guarantee users avoid admin approval; the tenant's policy and the scopes decide.
With microsoft_cloud set to gcc_high you register in the US Government cloud, which is a Microsoft national cloud, and publisher verification isn't available there.
Composio's Outlook toolkit also supports S2S_OAUTH2 (app-only access). Graph's application permissions, such as Mail.Read for all mailboxes, always need admin consent.
